Which MAVLink messages the Copter, Plane, QuadPlane and helicopter builds send with no stream request, counted on the ground (60 s) and in flight (30 s): Copter and the helicopter send only 7 message types (heartbeat, home position, GPS origin, time sync, parameter echo, mission-item-reached, status text); Plane and QuadPlane send 38, including attitude, position, GPS, battery, RC channels, airspeed, EKF status, vibration and wind, at roughly 1.7 Hz on the ground and 2.3 Hz in flight. The firmware source (GCS_MAVLink_Parameters.cpp) sets the default stream rate to 1 Hz for ArduPlane and 0 for Copter and helicopter builds, confirming this is intentional default behaviour, not a simulator artefact; the measured rate above the nominal 1 Hz was not explained. One run per vehicle, no stream requests sent, no GCS heartbeat sent.

Every MAV_CMD the vehicle source handles (from case labels in GCS_Common.cpp and each vehicle's own GCS_MAVLink_*.cpp) sent as COMMAND_LONG and COMMAND_INT with all parameters zero to a disarmed Copter, Plane, QuadPlane and helicopter: 87 or 88 commands each, result and vehicle text kept (command-sweep-final/command-sweep.csv). Found along the way: MAV_CMD_DO_CHANGE_ALTITUDE sent with all-zero parameters is never acknowledged on ArduPlane/QuadPlane and stops the MAVLink command channel acknowledging anything sent after it on the same link; the process does not crash while this is happening (it answers HEARTBEAT and stays alive for at least 120 s of further waiting, sitl-isolate-replay-crash.py), but panics when the hung process is terminated (SIGTERM): "PANIC: Should not be called on invalid location: Location cannot be (0, 0, 0)" in Location::get_alt_cm (AP_Common/Location.cpp:152), a SITL-only defensive check. Isolated black-box, without a debugger: an 180 s idle run with no commands sent never panics (isolate-idle-crash); single isolated sends of MAV_CMD_DO_CHANGE_ALTITUDE and MAV_CMD_DO_CHANGE_SPEED show only the altitude command gets no acknowledgement (isolate-change-altitude-crash); a replay of the sweep's first 16 commands followed by 120 s idle shows the hang begins exactly at that command and the panic only appears in the log after the final kill (isolate-replay-crash). Four earlier sweep attempts that sent that command mid-list and so lost the rest of the vehicle's results to the hang are kept (mavlink-command-sweep, -rerun, -with-defaults, -retry); the final sweep excludes it (listed as "NOT SENT" with the explanation) and so has genuine answers for every other command. Simulator only; results can depend on command order (the order used is the command number). Resolved from source, without a debugger: ArduPlane/GCS_MAVLink_Plane.cpp:handle_command_int_DO_CHANGE_ALTITUDE always builds Location{lat=0, lng=0, altitude_cm, frame} (the command is deliberately altitude-only, so it never sets a horizontal position) and calls get_alt_cm() on it; when the altitude sent is also 0, as in the all-zero sweep, that Location is the literal (0, 0, 0) the SITL-only check rejects. Confirmed: MAV_CMD_DO_CHANGE_ALTITUDE with a real altitude (50 m, both forms) is ACCEPTED immediately, the process exits cleanly afterwards, and a follow-up command on the same link is still answered; altitude 0 reproduces the hang and panic again, side by side in the same test (sitl-evidence/confirm-change-altitude-nonzero/). So the command itself is not broken: only a request with an explicit altitude of exactly 0 triggers this, in both the LONG and INT forms.

Six QuadPlane failsafe scenarios (GCS link loss, battery low, GPS loss, RC loss) at VTOL, transition, cruise and landing phases, on the simulator's VTOL takeoff/transition/waypoints/land mission. GCS link loss during the transition works (RTL). Battery-low did not trigger at all in either phase tested, unlike the equivalent Plane-only test; resolved separately: default_params/quadplane.parm never sets BATT_MONITOR (compiled default Type::NONE), so no battery was monitored; with it set (after a reboot, since it is an enable-flag parameter) the failsafe fired in 1.2 s, RTL, confirming the gap was in the stock quadplane.parm, not the firmware.
